A deterministic per-(trace, lane) sampling instant in microseconds that splits a trajectory into a warmup prefix and a profiled live set.

Per-(trace, lane) t* drawn from WindowTStarSampler with a lane-salted SHA-256 seed; warmup and profiling share the same draw (not a new sample). LaneHandoff still records the instance's t_star_us plus frontier state the seed alone cannot reproduce.
Largest arrival_offset_us across the resolved trace graph's nodes; zero when no node carries timing metadata.
Window policy for t*: t* = uniform(min×dur, max×dur) when the window is open; otherwise an exact instant with no RNG draw.

The set of `{nid}_out` channels for nodes that survived the t* chop; only input requirements targeting those channels are kept.
After chop_trie_at_tstar, survivor LlmNode prompt/segment paths still include the full pre-t* prefix so materialization rebuilds the exact resume prompt.
Extended warmup that replays post-t* remainders on pressure lanes for a duration budget, building KV load before profiling handoff.

slides.caption: Warm history first; measure from the frontier.
slides.lede: A recorded multi-turn trace arrives with cold prefix and cold KV. Graph warmup exists so profiling can measure from a mid-trace frontier — not from an empty cache.
slides.narration: Graph runs often care about mid-trace resume, not cold-start TTFT. Without warmup, every lane starts with a cold prefix and empty server KV. Trajectory t* warmup builds that history first, then profiles from the live frontier.
points: Cold start: empty server KV and a cold prompt prefix on every lane.
Graph profiling often wants steady mid-trace behavior, not first-token cold start.
Evidence: `rust/runtime/src/graph/tstar.rs` — t* splits firings into a warmup prefix and a profiled set.

slides.caption: Phase warmup burns requests; t* chops a trajectory.
slides.lede: Ordinary `--warmup-request-count` / duration phases burn requests and discard metrics. Trajectory `t*` partitions one recorded graph into a warmup prefix and a live profiling set.
slides.narration: Ordinary warmup is a separate phase that sends N requests or runs for a duration, then throws those metrics away. Trajectory t* is different: it chops a recorded multi-turn graph at a deterministic instant so the same plan warms and profiles one trajectory.
points: `--warmup-request-count` / duration phases warm the system, then discard warmup metrics.
`t*` partitions a recorded trajectory: arrivals before `t*` are history; arrivals at/after `t*` are the live set.
Keep three ideas distinct: phase warmup, trajectory chop, and later cache-pressure handoff.
Evidence: `docs/tutorials/warmup.md`; `rust/runtime/src/graph/tstar.rs`.

slides.caption: duration = max arrival · window = ratios × duration.
slides.lede: `trace_duration_us` is the max `arrival_offset_us` across nodes. The sampling window is `[trajectory_start_min_ratio, trajectory_start_max_ratio] × duration`.
slides.narration: Before drawing t*, the runtime measures how long the recorded trajectory spans — the latest arrival across nodes, or zero when no node carries timing. Config ratios then scale that duration into a closed sampling window for the t* draw.
points: `trace_duration_us` = max node `arrival_offset_us` (else `0.0`).
Window bounds: `lo = trajectory_start_min_ratio × duration`, `hi = trajectory_start_max_ratio × duration`.
Default ratios `[0, 0]` collapse the window to an exact instant at the start.
Evidence: `rust/runtime/src/graph/tstar.rs` — `trace_duration_us`, `WindowTStarSampler`.

slides.caption: Open window draws · collapsed window is exact.
slides.lede: `WindowTStarSampler` draws uniformly in `[lo, hi]`. Non-positive duration or `hi ≤ lo` returns an exact instant — float microseconds, no integer truncation.
slides.narration: When the trajectory duration is positive and the window upper bound is strictly above the lower bound, t* is a uniform random instant inside that open window. Otherwise the sampler returns an exact instant: zero for a non-positive duration, or the clamped lower bound when the window collapses — including the default ratios that pin both ends at zero.
points: Open window: `NumpyPcg64` uniform in `[lo, hi]`, then `t.max(0.0)` — float µs, no integer truncation.
`duration_us ≤ 0` → `0.0`; `hi ≤ lo` → `lo.max(0.0)` with no draw.
Knobs feed the sampler: `trajectory_start_*_ratio` and `t_star_random_seed`.
Evidence: `rust/runtime/src/graph/tstar.rs` — `WindowTStarSampler::sample_t_star`.

slides.caption: t_star_random_seed · salted per (trace, lane) · PCG64.
slides.lede: `seed_for_trace_lane` hashes `"{base}:{trace_id}:{lane}"` (SHA-256, first 8 bytes BE). Base is `t_star_random_seed` — decorrelated per trace and lane.
slides.narration: Each open-window draw salts the dedicated t* random seed with the trace id and lane index. The salted string is hashed, and the digest becomes the per-lane RNG seed. Same seed and inputs always reproduce the same t*; different traces or lanes decorrelate.
points: Formula: `SHA256("{base}:{trace_id}:{lane}")` → low 8 bytes BE → `u64` seed.
Base seed is config `t_star_random_seed` (not the run-root `random_seed`).
Open draws use `NumpyPcg64::from_u64_seed(seed).uniform(lo, hi)`.
Evidence: `rust/runtime/src/graph/tstar.rs` — `seed_for_trace_lane`.

slides.caption: n0 · n1 dropped · START → n2 · n3 live.
slides.lede: `chop_trie_at_tstar` drops `arrival_offset_us < t*`, then re-roots survivors that lost all predecessors from `START` with `min_start_delay_us = arrival − t*`.
slides.narration: The snapshot chop removes every node whose arrival is strictly before t*. Survivors that still have a surviving predecessor keep their inter-turn edge. Survivors that lost all real predecessors get a synthetic start edge whose delay is the residual arrival minus t*. Edges between survivors stay as recorded.

`t* ≤ 0` returns the graph unchanged (full replay).

slides.caption: No await on chopped sources · avoid deadlocks.
slides.lede: Survivors must not await `{src}_out` channels from dropped predecessors — that would deadlock `await_inputs`. The chop keeps only requirements whose source survives.
slides.narration: Fan-in nodes wait on named output channels from their predecessors. After the chop, a dropped predecessor never writes that channel. The chop keeps only input requirements whose source still exists — a fully re-rooted node can end with no remaining inputs.
points: Dropped predecessors never write `{src}_out` post-chop.
Keep only `inputs` requirements whose channel is in the survivor out-set.
A node re-rooted entirely from `START` may end with empty `inputs`.

slides.caption: Chop · recycle under pressure · then drain.
slides.lede: Cache-pressure warmup is the extended phase: lanes recycle chopped post-`t*` graphs against the server so KV stays under load before the handoff drain.
slides.narration: After the boundary chop, duration-bounded lanes repeatedly dispatch pressure templates — each plan is the post-t* remainder at that lane's salted t*. The goal is cache pressure: keep the inference server's KV busy with live frontier traffic until the clock deadline, then drain into the handoff.
points: `GraphPressureRecycle` runs until Clock deadline; lanes share one corpus cursor.
Each dispatch uses the lane-salted `t*` chop of a pressure template (post-`t*` live set).
Distinct from ordinary phase warmup and from the later profiling resume.
Evidence: `rust/runtime/src/engine/graph_phase_runtime.rs` — `GraphPressureRecycle`; `snapshot.rs` extended-warmup docs.

slides.caption: t* uses t_star_random_seed · recycle uses run-root random_seed.
slides.lede: `PermutationDraw` remaps the shared corpus cursor: Sequential (`x % n`), Shuffle (persistent epoch), or Random (MT19937 choice). Shuffle/Random child seeds derive from run-root `random_seed` — not `t_star_random_seed`.
slides.narration: Pressure and profiling share one strategy-aware corpus draw. Sequential walks the corpus in order. Shuffle uses a persistent without-replacement epoch. Random picks with replacement. Those child seeds come from the run-root random seed — explicitly not from the dedicated t* seed, which only salts per-lane t* draws.
points: Modes: `Sequential` · `Shuffle` · `Random` (`GraphSamplingStrategy` / `RecycleDrawMode`).
Shuffle child seed: `SHA256("{root}:dataset.sampler.shuffle")` → NumPy PCG64 epochs.
Random child seed: `SHA256("{root}:dataset.sampler.random")` → Python MT19937 — root is `random_seed`, not `t_star_random_seed`.
Evidence: `rust/runtime/src/graph/tstar.rs` — `sampler_shuffle_seed` / `sampler_random_seed`; `graph_input.rs` — `TStarWindow::recycle_draw`.
